protocol.description:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.
This protocol allows a privileged DDE client such as the dock or shell to control and observe the compositor's multitaskview (workspace overview) mode. In multitaskview mode the compositor presents an overview of all windows and workspaces so the user can switch between them.
The compositor should reject bind attempts from non-privileged clients.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

interface.name: treeland_multitaskview_v2
interface.description:
A global that provides read/write access to the compositor's multitaskview mode state.
The compositor should reject bind attempts from non-privileged clients.
On binding, the compositor immediately sends a state event carrying the current mode so that the client starts synchronized.
The client sends set_state to request a mode transition. The compositor applies the transition at its discretion and confirms the new state via a state event. The compositor may also emit state spontaneously when the mode changes through other means (e.g. a keyboard shortcut or gesture).

entry.name: normal
entry.summary: multitaskview is not shown; windows are presented normally

request.name: destroy
set_state
request.description:
Request that the compositor transition to the given multitaskview mode. The compositor may ignore the request or apply it asynchronously. If the mode changes, the compositor confirms the new state by emitting a state event.
Sending the same mode that is already active is a no-op; the compositor need not emit a state event in response.

event.name: state
event.description:
Emitted by the compositor whenever the multitaskview mode changes, including once immediately after the client binds this interface to convey the initial state.
The compositor emits this event both in response to a set_state request and when the mode changes through any other compositor-side mechanism.
